subject: Mutual commitment checklist, acceptance tests, and fail-mode playbook
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@healthgrid.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot scope and next steps (HealthGrid)

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency and the observability dashboard. Procurement asked that we put a short mutual commitment checklist together so internal stakeholders can sign off on a short pilot. Key asks from our side:

- Confirmation of data handling (KMS + retention policy) and SOC2 evidence.
- A concise MAP with milestones, owners, and signoff points (we prefer weekly checkpoints for a 4-week eval).
- Clear acceptance tests (latency, error rate, cost per 1k requests) and what constitutes failure/rollback.

Can you send a single doc with those items and an initial proposed acceptance-test matrix? Procurement will attach this to our internal approval.

Elena
Elena Morales
Director of Product, HealthGrid
elena@healthgrid.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Mutual commitment checklist + eval proving playbook (draft)

Elena — thanks, and great meeting. Attached are two artifacts: a MAP spreadsheet (MAP_HealthGrid_v1.xlsx) and a short PDF with proposed smoke/evaluation test cases (eval-testcases.pdf). High-level summary below.

Proposal (4-week eval; 3 acceptance gates):

1) Gate A — Basic connectivity & security (Week 1)
   - Success criteria: Private VPC peering established, KMS integration verified, SOC2 evidence packet delivered.
   - Tests: KMS round-trip key-wrap test, sample logs forwarded to your SIEM, penetration test report stub.
   - Accept/Fail: Fail if KMS integration or VPC cannot be validated within 72 hours after handoff.

2) Gate B — Functional baseline (Weeks 2–3)
   - Success criteria: 95% generation success rate on canonical prompts, median latency <= 220ms p50 for baseline seq length, cost projection within agreed threshold (< $25 per 1k gen tokens for pilot profile).
   - Tests: 200 canonical prompts run, automated concordance checks, random sample human review (10/200).
   - Accept/Fail: Fail if success rate <92% or latency p50 > 300ms for two consecutive days.

3) Gate C — Production mimic & go/no-go (Week 4)
   - Success criteria: 99% uptime (scheduled maintenance excluded), end-to-end SLA smoke test pass, rollout plan verified with canary traffic.
   - Tests: 2-hour ramp to 2x expected pilot traffic with KV-cache enabled, fallback exercised to smaller model (<10% of requests), end-to-end tracing verified.
   - Accept/Fail: Fail if canary fails more than twice or critical errors exceed 0.5% of token responses in a 24h window.

Fail-mode playbook (short):
- Immediate rollback to previous model variant and notify stakeholders.
- Root-cause triage: infra, model, prompt drift, or data quality.
- Remediation window: 48h patch, otherwise pilot is paused and re-scoped.

Owners and signoff cadence (see MAP spreadsheet):
- Redwood lead: Ben Carter — infra & rollout
- Redwood test owner: Karthik Iyer — test runs and telemetry
- HealthGrid product owner: Elena Morales — acceptance signoff
- Weekly checkpoint: Friday 10am PT (15 min)

Attachments: MAP_HealthGrid_v1.xlsx (milestones + owners), eval-testcases.pdf (detailed runbook).

Can Marissa and Ben scan the acceptance thresholds below and flag anything that's operationally unrealistic? Elena — if the thresholds look reasonable we can push this to your procurement as the mutual commitment doc.

Thanks,

Soojin Lee
Head of Platform Partnerships, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

--
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Elena Morales <elena@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T14:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual commitment checklist + eval proving playbook (draft)

Quick notes from an ops perspective — solid draft. Two suggested changes to make acceptance binary and easily auditable: 

- Change the Week 2 success trigger to require a fixed test harness SHA and test dataset snapshot (we'll attach the reference dataset in the Drive link). That prevents drift between runs.
- For the latency threshold, use p50 and p95 bands with a flag for degradation: pass if p50 <=220ms AND p95 <=450ms over 24h. If p95 spikes above 600ms for >30m, trigger immediate rollback.

Also adding an explicit security signoff: Redwood security will provide the SOC2 evidence packet by Day 3 of Week 1; HealthGrid to confirm receipt. If any audit gap remains open at Gate A, Gate A is delayed but not failed; we allow a 72h remediation window before hard fail.

I'll drop a quick comment in the MAP spreadsheet on owners and test dataset links.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

--

Subject: Re: Mutual commitment checklist + eval proving playbook (draft)

Thanks — this looks actionable and detailed, appreciate the concrete thresholds. Procurement reviewed and wants one small tweak before we circulate internally: replace the open-ended remediation window language with explicit timelines and escalation points (you already have 48h remediation; please add who will be the escalation contact at 24h).

If Redwood can add the 24h escalation contact into Gate B and Gate C failure rows we will route this with procurement today. Once that's in, I will attach MAP_HealthGrid_v1.xlsx to our approval packet and route for internal signatures.

We are OK to proceed on the following basis:
- Redwood will share SOC2 artifact by 2026-11-07 17:00 PT.
- Redwood test owner (Karthik) will run first canonical test harness on 2026-11-09 morning PT.
- Weekly checkpoint Fridays (first is 2026-11-12).

Please confirm and add the 24h escalation contact lines.

Elena
Elena Morales
